answers.answer:
Release context: SCOPe 2.08 (stable; latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16). Both domains sit in the same lineage: class a (All alpha, sunid 46456) > fold a.4 'DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical bundle' (46688) > superfamily a.4.1 'Homeodomain-like' (46689) > family a.4.1.1 'Homeodomain' (46690) > protein 'Engrailed Homeodomain' (46691) > species Drosophila melanogaster [TaxId 7227] (46692). d1p7jd_ is sunid 94286 (1p7j chain D; comment 'complexed with nhe; mutant'; PDB title 'Crystal structure of engrailed homeodomain mutant K52E'; X-ray 2.1 Å, R 0.20, SPACI/AEROSPACI 0.44, good WHAT_CHECK scores). d1ztra1 is sunid 125655 (1ztr A:0-59; comment 'mutant'; PDB title 'Solution structure of Engrailed homeodomain L16A mutant', keywords 'denatured state, protein folding, folding intermediate'; NMR, SPACI 0.0024, very poor WHAT_CHECK packing/Ramachandran/chi/backbone Z-scores). The SCOPe sequences confirm they are near-identical point mutants of the same 60-residue Engrailed homeodomain: d1ztra1 carries L16A (…LARAKREF…) and d1p7jd_ carries K52E (…QNERAK…), and d1p7jd_ is a shorter 53-residue construct lacking the N-terminal arm residues present in d1ztra1. 1ztr also carries a one-residue artifact domain d1ztra2 (l.1.1.1, residue -1, an expression-tag remnant) that is not part of the homeodomain.

What the hf flag means and what homology remains justified. The /homology endpoint for d1ztra1 reports homology_implied_by_level true (scope px) but lists a domain-scoped, non-inherited heterogeneity record 'hf: heterogeneous fold; applies to domains that adopt a different fold than the exemplar domain but has similar sequence and number of secondary structures'. d1p7jd_ has no such record. In SCOPe, family and superfamily membership are statements about common ancestry inferred primarily from sequence and from the protein/species node, not a certification that every deposited coordinate set adopts the exemplar fold. For these two domains the homology inference is as strong as it ever gets: same gene, same species, >90% sequence identity to each other and to wild-type Engrailed HD, differing by single engineered substitutions. Family-level (a.4.1.1) and superfamily-level (a.4.1) homology, and the inference that the native protein adopts the 3-helical bundle fold, therefore remain fully justified for the underlying sequence of d1ztra1. What is NOT justified is reading the a.4 fold label as a description of the 1ztr coordinates: the hf flag records that the deposited L16A NMR model does not adopt the exemplar fold even though sequence and secondary-structure count are similar. The fold assignment of d1ztra1 is inherited by lineage from its parent protein node, not earned by structural similarity; the class/fold labels describe the family exemplar, not this model. The flag is domain-scoped and not inherited, so it says nothing adverse about d1p7jd_, the other 1p7j chains, the Engrailed protein node, or the family.

Why they are not interchangeable templates. (1) d1ztra1 is a destabilized-core mutant (L16A removes a conserved hydrophobic-core leucine) solved by NMR as a denatured-state/folding-intermediate ensemble; using it as a comparative-modelling template for any homeodomain would propagate a non-native conformation into the model, regardless of high sequence identity. d1p7jd_ is a native-like 2.1 Å crystal structure in a DNA complex and is a legitimate template for the folded homeodomain; its K52E substitution lies in the DNA-recognition helix 3 region, so even it should not be used to transfer wild-type DNA-binding specificity or affinity without checking the literature. (2) Quality and representative selection: SPACI 0.0024 versus 0.44 means d1ztra1 would never be selected as an ASTRAL representative for the family, protein, or species node; d1p7jd_ or another high-resolution Engrailed/Antennapedia structure would be. Any pipeline that picks 'a representative a.4.1.1 domain' must respect this ranking and should exclude hf-flagged domains. (3) Training examples: for a structure-based fold classifier, d1ztra1 is a label/structure mismatch (label a.4, coordinates not a.4-like); including it as a positive a.4 example injects noise, and including the pair (d1ztra1, d1p7jd_) as a 'same-family therefore structurally similar' positive pair for structural-alignment or TM-score benchmarks is wrong because they will superpose poorly. For a sequence-based classifier the pair is fine but nearly redundant (same protein), so it inflates apparent accuracy. hf-flagged domains should be filtered from structure-based training/test sets, or retained only with their heterogeneity record as metadata. (4) Boundaries differ (A:0-59 vs the shorter chain D construct), and 1ztr contains an l.1.1.1 artifact domain that must not be merged into the homeodomain sequence. (5) Function transfer: both are 'mutant' entries; SCOPe records that fact in comments but does not record functional consequences, so neither structure should be used to assert wild-type Engrailed function, and the folding-intermediate model in particular has no native DNA-binding geometry to transfer.

External evidence needed beyond SCOPe: the primary publication for 1ztr (Religa, Markson, Mayor, Freund & Fersht, Nature 2005, the solution structure of an Engrailed HD denatured state/folding intermediate) and for 1p7j (K52E engrailed HD/DNA complex) to confirm the biophysical status of each mutant; secondary-structure and superposition analysis (e.g., DSSP and TM-score/FATCAT against wild-type 1enh) to quantify how far the 1ztr ensemble departs from the 3-helical bundle; and UniProt (Engrailed, P02836) and Pfam PF00046 for wild-type sequence and domain boundaries. The SCOPe 2.08 API returned empty uniprot/pfam/pubmed xrefs for both domains, so those cross-references are from prior knowledge, not verified here.
evidence_used: pretrained knowledge: Religa et al. 2005 Nature (1ztr L16A En-HD folding intermediate); UniProt P02836; Pfam PF00046

answers.answer:
Release context: SCOPe 2.08 (stable; latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16). Both domains sit in the same lineage: class a (All alpha, sunid 46456) > fold a.4 'DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical bundle' (46688) > superfamily a.4.1 'Homeodomain-like' (46689) > family a.4.1.1 'Homeodomain' (46690) > protein 'Engrailed Homeodomain' (46691) > species Drosophila melanogaster [TaxId 7227] (46692). d1p7jd_ is sunid 94286 (1p7j chain D; comment 'complexed with nhe; mutant'; PDB title 'Crystal structure of engrailed homeodomain mutant K52E'; X-ray 2.1 Å, R 0.20, SPACI/AEROSPACI 0.44, good WHAT_CHECK scores). d1ztra1 is sunid 125655 (1ztr A:0-59; comment 'mutant'; PDB title 'Solution structure of Engrailed homeodomain L16A mutant', keywords 'denatured state, protein folding, folding intermediate'; NMR, SPACI 0.0024, very poor WHAT_CHECK packing/Ramachandran/chi/backbone Z-scores). The SCOPe sequences confirm they are near-identical point mutants of the same 60-residue Engrailed homeodomain: d1ztra1 carries L16A (…LARAKREF…) and d1p7jd_ carries K52E (…QNERAK…), and d1p7jd_ is a shorter 53-residue construct lacking the N-terminal arm residues present in d1ztra1. 1ztr also carries a one-residue artifact domain d1ztra2 (l.1.1.1, residue -1, an expression-tag remnant) that is not part of the homeodomain.

What the hf flag means and what homology remains justified. The /homology endpoint for d1ztra1 reports homology_implied_by_level true (scope px) but lists a domain-scoped, non-inherited heterogeneity record 'hf: heterogeneous fold; applies to domains that adopt a different fold than the exemplar domain but has similar sequence and number of secondary structures'. d1p7jd_ has no such record. In SCOPe, family and superfamily membership are statements about common ancestry inferred primarily from sequence and from the protein/species node, not a certification that every deposited coordinate set adopts the exemplar fold. For these two domains the homology inference is as strong as it ever gets: same gene, same species, >90% sequence identity to each other and to wild-type Engrailed HD, differing by single engineered substitutions. Family-level (a.4.1.1) and superfamily-level (a.4.1) homology, and the inference that the native protein adopts the 3-helical bundle fold, therefore remain fully justified for the underlying sequence of d1ztra1. What is NOT justified is reading the a.4 fold label as a description of the 1ztr coordinates: the hf flag records that the deposited L16A NMR model does not adopt the exemplar fold even though sequence and secondary-structure count are similar. The fold assignment of d1ztra1 is inherited by lineage from its parent protein node, not earned by structural similarity; the class/fold labels describe the family exemplar, not this model. The flag is domain-scoped and not inherited, so it says nothing adverse about d1p7jd_, the other 1p7j chains, the Engrailed protein node, or the family.

Why they are not interchangeable templates. (1) d1ztra1 is a destabilized-core mutant (L16A removes a conserved hydrophobic-core leucine) solved by NMR as a denatured-state/folding-intermediate ensemble; using it as a comparative-modelling template for any homeodomain would propagate a non-native conformation into the model, regardless of high sequence identity. d1p7jd_ is a native-like 2.1 Å crystal structure in a DNA complex and is a legitimate template for the folded homeodomain; its K52E substitution lies in the DNA-recognition helix 3 region, so even it should not be used to transfer wild-type DNA-binding specificity or affinity without checking the literature. (2) Quality and representative selection: SPACI 0.0024 versus 0.44 means d1ztra1 would never be selected as an ASTRAL representative for the family, protein, or species node; d1p7jd_ or another high-resolution Engrailed/Antennapedia structure would be. Any pipeline that picks 'a representative a.4.1.1 domain' must respect this ranking and should exclude hf-flagged domains. (3) Training examples: for a structure-based fold classifier, d1ztra1 is a label/structure mismatch (label a.4, coordinates not a.4-like); including it as a positive a.4 example injects noise, and including the pair (d1ztra1, d1p7jd_) as a 'same-family therefore structurally similar' positive pair for structural-alignment or TM-score benchmarks is wrong because they will superpose poorly. For a sequence-based classifier the pair is fine but nearly redundant (same protein), so it inflates apparent accuracy. hf-flagged domains should be filtered from structure-based training/test sets, or retained only with their heterogeneity record as metadata. (4) Boundaries differ (A:0-59 vs the shorter chain D construct), and 1ztr contains an l.1.1.1 artifact domain that must not be merged into the homeodomain sequence. (5) Function transfer: both are 'mutant' entries; SCOPe records that fact in comments but does not record functional consequences, so neither structure should be used to assert wild-type Engrailed function, and the folding-intermediate model in particular has no native DNA-binding geometry to transfer.

External evidence needed beyond SCOPe: the primary publication for 1ztr (Religa, Markson, Mayor, Freund & Fersht, Nature 2005, the solution structure of an Engrailed HD denatured state/folding intermediate) and for 1p7j (K52E engrailed HD/DNA complex) to confirm the biophysical status of each mutant; secondary-structure and superposition analysis (e.g., DSSP and TM-score/FATCAT against wild-type 1enh) to quantify how far the 1ztr ensemble departs from the 3-helical bundle; and UniProt (Engrailed, P02836) and Pfam PF00046 for wild-type sequence and domain boundaries. The SCOPe 2.08 API returned empty uniprot/pfam/pubmed xrefs for both domains, so those cross-references are from prior knowledge, not verified here.
